StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so it adds -- which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236, no StackType branch). This is the CORRECT handling of Single; the census's 15 wrong units are the ones that override on_stack to `pass` (`py tools/audit/power_census.py stack`). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterPowerAmountChanged.rationale: C# hooks `AfterPowerAmountChanged(choiceContext, power, amount, applier, cardSource)` with four guards -- `applier != base.Owner`, `!power.Owner.IsPlayer`, `!(power is XPower)`, `amount >= 0m` -- and accumulates into a per-victim dictionary (PossessStrengthPower.cs:31-55 / PossessSpeedPower.cs:31-55). The sim reproduces all four in `_PossessPower._track` (powers.py:3092-3099: `applier is self.owner`, `target.side == "player"`, `name == self._stat_id`, `delta < 0`) and wires it to BOTH of the sim's power-change notifications, on_power_applied (powers.py:3101-3104) and on_power_amount_changed (powers.py:3106-3109). That double wiring is CORRECT and worth recording: C#'s single AfterPowerAmountChanged covers both the new-power and the stacking path, where the sim splits them (cmds.py:327 vs cmds.py:312), so hooking only one would have missed half the thefts. These two units are the ported READERS of the missing-`applier=` shape that appears all over half B -- which is why they had to be audited early -- and they are the reason it stays dormant there: the `applier is self.owner` AND player-target AND negative-delta conjunction excludes every applier-less enemy self-buff. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.rationale: C# returns the stolen total on the owner's real death: `foreach (var item in StolenStrength) PowerCmd.Apply<XPower>(choiceContext, item.Key, -item.Value, null, null)` (PossessStrengthPower.cs:57-67) -- note `applier: null`, deliberately, so the give-back does not re-enter this power's own tracker. powers.py:3114-3120 does the same with `PowerCmd.apply(self.hooks, target, self._stat_power(), -amount)` and no applier, then clears the dict and expires. Two things checked. (1) The SIGN: the tracker stores negative deltas, so `-amount` is a positive give-back on both sides. (2) The give-back's own applier is None on both sides, which is what keeps `_track` from re-firing -- and it is also why the sim's `-amount` re-application does NOT hit power_cmd gap G1's sign-aware Artifact hole: the target is the player, the amount is positive, and the census's typing finding shows only strength/dexterity flip and only at a negative amount. Faithful. The sim's added `self._expire()` matches C#'s CreatureCmd.cs:533 power strip in net effect. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
powers.py:3096 `target.side == "player"`. Identical, and load-bearing: it is what stops the power tracking the Dexterity it drains from another enemy.

guards.what: The per-victim dictionary keyed by Creature
guards.rationale: `Dictionary<Creature, decimal>` vs `dict[Creature, int]` (powers.py:3090). One key in single-player; the shape is preserved rather than flattened, which is the right call.

PowerStackType.Single and the tracker uses the dictionary, not base.Amount, so the on_stack question is inert here on both sides. The owner is monsters/glory/the_lost_and_forgotten.py (The Forgotten).
